flawed_step: Step 3: the claim that 3-regularity plus 3-connectivity forces a spanning cycle. No known result supports it: degree 3 is far below the Dirac/Ore thresholds, and Tutte's theorem needs planarity and 4-connectivity. The step is in fact false.
counterexample: The Petersen graph (outer 5-cycle u0..u4, inner pentagram v0v2v4v1v3, spokes uivi). It is simple, 3-regular, has 10 vertices and vertex connectivity 3, and is non-Hamiltonian. The Tutte graph is a planar counterexample.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The Petersen graph is 3-regular and 3-connected under the given definition (at least 4 vertices, still connected after deleting any 2 vertices), but it has no Hamiltonian cycle. Such a cycle would use an even number of spokes (2 or 4), and each case forces a contradiction in the complementary perfect matching. The attempted proof fails at the step that needs to derive Hamiltonicity from degree 3 and 3-connectivity alone.
